description:
FOUND 2026-08-21 while fixing the LEAPR temperature-block-selection bug
(generate_tape used deck block 0 regardless of the requested temperature).

THE HAZARD. leapr::generate::cached_tape_path keys its on-disk cache
(~/.cache/outram-park/endf/leapr-generated/) on a GenerationRecipe made of:
material, deck source, deck sha256, evaluation date field, physical-constant
vintage, temperature, and elastic-channel choice. It does NOT include anything
identifying the GENERATOR -- no crate version, no build id, no hash of the
LEAPR code path. So when the port's own physics changes, every previously
cached tape stays valid by that key and keeps being served.

OBSERVED, concretely. After fixing the block-selection bug I re-measured
H-in-H2O at 293.6 K through thermal_scattering_tape() and got the OLD, wrong
numbers back (T_eff 1195.35 K). The tape being read was
HinH2O-293.6000K-d09297bc57c0de2f.endf, written 2026-08-19 23:47 -- before the
fix. Deleting it and regenerating gave T_eff 1194.33 K. Nothing warned; the
recipe hash was unchanged because the deck, constants and temperature were
unchanged. Only the code was different, and the code is not in the key.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS ONE FIX. This is a silent-stale-result mechanism
that survives across sessions and machines: a developer who fixes a kernel bug,
re-runs the suite and sees it pass may be seeing pre-fix cached data. It also
cuts the other way -- a REGRESSION would be masked on any machine with a warm
cache. It is exactly the failure mode the crate's own porting notes warn about
(a plausible number rather than an error).

Note the tests still passed both before and after the fix here, because their
tolerances (2 %) were wider than the bug (0.6 %). That is luck, not protection.

SUGGESTED FIX (not done -- raising rather than guessing at the right key):
  1. Add a generator identity to GenerationRecipe. Cheapest credible version is
     env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") plus a manually-bumped GENERATOR_REVISION const
     that any change to the LEAPR generation path must increment. A build-script
     hash over src/leapr/ would be automatic but adds build complexity -- the
     maintainer should pick.
  2. Whichever is chosen, write it into the .recipe sidecar (already emitted)
     so a stale artifact is diagnosable by reading the file.
  3. Consider an escape hatch env var to bypass/purge the cache for a run.

WORKAROUND UNTIL THEN: rm -rf ~/.cache/outram-park/endf/leapr-generated/ after
any change to the LEAPR generation path, before trusting a measurement.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
FIXED 2026-08-21, commit 5a91ecf7, per the maintainer's explicit design
(GH #27 comment): a CachePolicy enum, not an automatic key fix.

CachePolicy::{AlwaysRegenerate, UseCacheIfAvailable} on SabRequest.cache,
set via with_cache(). AlwaysRegenerate is the default -- every request
computes fresh and never touches the on-disk cache at all (no read, no
write). UseCacheIfAvailable reuses a hit (log::warn! naming the staleness
risk and pointing at #27 on every hit), and falls back to generating fresh
-- never an error -- on a miss, populating the cache for next time.

Also bumped GENERATOR_REVISION 2 -> 3: the temperature-block-selection fix
(1a904fc5) changed output for HInH2O/DInD2O/OInD2O and should have bumped
it then but didn't. Documented as the concrete case study in the
constant's own doc comment, since GENERATOR_REVISION still exists and
still matters for UseCacheIfAvailable users -- the new policy doesn't
replace it, it makes the risk that mechanism can't fully close an explicit
opt-in instead.

Two new tests prove the actual bug scenario: one plants a deliberately
invalid tape under the real cache key and confirms AlwaysRegenerate never
reads it; the other confirms UseCacheIfAvailable falls back gracefully on
a miss and populates the cache.

Full njoy suite green (0 failures, 24 targets); workspace check clean;
clippy clean on the change.

title: njoy LEAPR: regeneration cache key omits the generator, so a physics fix keeps serving stale tapes

description:
CONTEXT: on 2026-08-11 the crate was relicensed Apache-2.0 -> GPL-3.0-only (see crate NOTICE) and a SISO port of the GNU Octave control package's c2d/d2c/tf/filt core landed in src/lib/beta_testing/z_domain/ (upstream gnu-octave/pkg-control commit f39e2625bffc56864c3af746b4410bb71ce6bbb1, GPLv3-or-later side only; the BSD-3 SLICOT kernels were NOT ported). Implemented and verified (11 tests, methodology + measured results in verification_tests.rs doc comments): Zoh, Tustin, TustinPrewarp, MatchedPoleZero c2d; Tustin, TustinPrewarp, MatchedPoleZero d2c; O(1) DF2T discrete stepping.

DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT, in scope for this bead:
1. d2c by zero-order hold — upstream inst/@ss/__d2c__.m computes it with a matrix logarithm (logm of the augmented [A B; 0 I] matrix). Needs a general dense matrix log; not half-implemented.
2. c2d by first-order hold (foh) and impulse-invariant methods — upstream inst/@ss/__c2d__.m (foh via augmented matrix exponential) and imp_invar.m.
3. System order > 2 for Zoh and MatchedPoleZero — currently ZDomainError::UnsupportedOrder, because poles/zeros come from the quadratic formula. General order needs a polynomial root finder (companion-matrix eigenvalues) and/or a scaling-and-squaring expm. Tustin variants already handle any order.
4. Consider whether z_domain should be wired into the controllers layer (a discrete PID via c2d of the analog PID) and whether TUAS-facing alpha_nightly needs a twin — currently z_domain exists in beta_testing only, documented in crate CLAUDE.md.

LICENCE RULE for any follow-up: per-file provenance. If a follow-up ports SLICOT-derived material (anything under slicot-reference/ or the __sl_* kernels), that file's BSD 3-Clause notice must be carried verbatim; do not relabel it GPL. See crate NOTICE.
title: chem-eng: z-domain follow-ups — d2c ZOH (matrix log), c2d foh/impulse-invariant, order > 2 support

description:
Maintainer request, 2026-08-13 (filed outside active hours; no code work done).

Need steel property correlations that remain valid up to 1200 C, for high-temperature HTGR/HTR-10 component modelling (hot gas duct, SG tubing, vessel internals, accident-envelope temperatures).

Scope when picked up during active hours (search-before-building rule applies -- do NOT write new correlations before checking):
- Check outram-park-fork-offbeat's material-property library (~70 correlations, incl. cladding/structural steels) for existing steel property sets and their stated validity ranges.
- Check tuas_boussinesq_solver's solid material enum (SolidMaterial / steel variants) -- what upper temperature bound do the existing steel correlations actually claim?
- Check tampines and outram-foam-basic-lib thermophysics/solid-thermo layers for a second implementation before adding a third.
Then: extend or add the needed properties (density, specific heat, thermal conductivity, and thermal expansion / mechanical properties if required) with sourced, cited correlations covering up to 1200 C.

Open questions for the maintainer:
- WHICH steel(s)? (e.g. SS316/316H, SS304, Alloy 800H, 2.25Cr-1Mo / Incoloy) -- 1200 C is above the practical service range of most austenitic stainless, so this is likely an accident-envelope requirement rather than a service one.
- Which properties are needed (thermal only, or mechanical/creep too)?
- Data must come from open/public literature per DATA_POLICY.md, catalogued into kovan with its access tier.

Related: op-szmi.6 (replace invented htgr_sim_v1 geometry with sourced HTR-10 values).

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
SCOPE WIDENED by maintainer, 2026-08-13: the properties must be usable inside htgr_sim_v1, and the sim is currently CRASHING AT LOW TEMPERATURES (see op-m1jz, P1).

So this is no longer a high-temperature-only ask. The needed validity range spans ambient (~20-25 degC) through 1200 degC in one continuous, non-panicking correlation set. When selecting sources and correlations, check the LOW end explicitly -- that is what is breaking today; 1200 degC is the headroom requirement.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
CORRECTION, 2026-08-13 07:2x -- disregard the previous note claiming the LOW end (ambient) is what breaks. That was my wrong inference. Real trace is on op-m1jz.

The actual failure is the UPPER bound: the solid steel correlation used by htgr_sim_v1's hot gas duct / circulator tops out around 700 degC and throws ThermophysicalPropertyTemperatureRangeError above it. HTGR hot-leg helium runs ~750-950 degC, so the existing range is unfit for purpose.

So this bead is back to being exactly what it said originally -- HIGH-temperature properties, to 1200 degC -- and it is now on the critical path for a P1 crash rather than being forward-looking headroom. Priority raised accordingly.

The specific consumer to satisfy first: whichever SolidMaterial variant htgr_sim_v1 assigns to the hot gas duct and circulator.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
DONE 2026-08-13, pushed on develop (f565d31b, wired at 3acc9536).
SolidMaterial::SteelSS304LHighTemp, Kim ANL-75-55 solid-region equations over 300-1700 K -- comfortably past the
1200 degC = 1473 K this bead asked for. Verified against Kim's own published tables, 15 points each: density vs
Table 7 max deviation 0.0061%, cp vs Table 2 0.0341%, k vs Table 10 0.0370%, enthalpy vs Table 2 0.0049 cal/g,
enthalpy<->temperature round trip worst 4.5e-13 K.
Honest about its own limits: 300-1600 K is measured-data-backed, 1600-1700 K is Kim's extrapolation into the melting
range, and that distinction is in the docs. Out-of-range still ERRORS -- nothing clamped, 299 K and 1701 K both
asserted rejected. The old SteelSS304L is byte-unchanged so the CIET regression tests are untouched.
This is VERIFICATION against the source, not validation -- no independent 304L measurements, no human review.

title: Steel material properties valid to 1200 C (high-temperature envelope for HTGR components)
